answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-elapsed-time admission: each new identity must complete a trusted-timer countdown sealed in a secure enclave, a random wait of say ten real days, and only one such countdown can run per physical machine at a time. The timer is a crystal that cannot be fast-forwarded or run in parallel, so an operator stacking a thousand sybils on one box must serialize them, waiting ten thousand days, while buying a thousand separate machines instead costs a thousandfold. A fresh swarm stays a lifeless relic buried in the dune, aging out long before it can vote or earn.
